title: Blue Jays’ Dylan Cease named American League starter for All-Star Game
content:
SAN DIEGO — Blue Jays coaches wheeled a massive whiteboard into Toronto’s road clubhouse on Sunday morning. It was covered with an array of drawings, featuring cats and oysters and a simple message: Dylan Cease will be the American League’s starting pitcher at the 2026 All-Star Game.

Cease, manager John Schneider decided on Saturday night, will get the ball to begin his first-ever All-Star Game on Tuesday in Philadelphia. The righty, who leads AL pitchers in strikeouts, FIP and FanGraphs WAR, was selected for the honour over Yankees starter Cam Schlittler, who has since opted out of the game.

After signing a seven-year, $210 million deal with the Jays over the winter, Cease has been brilliant for Toronto. The organization spoke of attempting to tap into Cease’s ceiling after inking the righty, and he’s delivered on those high expectations thus far. In 17 starts, Cease has a 2.56 ERA with 148 strikeouts. He hasn’t allowed a run over his last two starts (15 innings pitched) and carried a no-hitter into the ninth earlier this week.

“The way it’s unfolded,” Schneider said, “especially the last couple in Seattle and then in San Fran, pretty dominant outings. Kind of shows everyone what he can do and why we were excited to sign him when he did. It’s worked out really, really well.”

There was a case for Schlittler to start the game, as the 25-year-old leads AL pitchers in ERA, Baseball Reference WAR and games started. Cease, after his latest start, acknowledged that Schlittler was certainly deserving. The decision came down to Schlittler and Cease, Schneider said Sunday, but the Blue Jays manager went with his guy. He earned the right to make that decision due to Toronto’s run to the World Series last year, beating the Yankees in the ALDS along the way.

“Whenever a guy’s leading the league in strikeouts in an era like right now,” Schneider said, “and you got really good stuff, you’re very representative of the American League.”

Schneider called New York manager Aaron Boone early on Sunday to inform him of the decision. He offered to talk through the decision with Schlittler and Boone. Shortly after, Schlittler opted out of pitching in the Midsummer Classic.

“If Cam was going to pitch,” Schneider said, “my decision was still going to be Dylan, after careful consideration.”

Cease was speechless, the righty said, when he found out the news. His teammates called for him to make a speech in the San Diego road clubhouse, but the strikeout artist didn’t have many words. He enjoyed the coach’s artistic display, a nod to the paintings he’s crafted throughout the season and gifted to many Jays staff members. Pete Walker, Schneider said, did some heavy lifting on the masterpiece, including drawing a cat with a top hat.

“They were missing a few things,” Cease said. “But, you know what, I’m being hypercritical. It was really cool.”

Cease will become the third Jays pitcher to start an All-Star Game alongside Dave Stieb and Roy Halladay. The righty will join Louis Varland and Ernie Clement at the 2026 All-Star Game, alongside Toronto’s entire coaching staff who earned the honour by making the World Series last fall. Vladimir Guerrero Jr. was voted into the All-Star Game, but opted out.
